_meta.indication: Vizamyl is indicated for PET imaging of the brain to estimate beta amyloid neuritic plaque density in adult patients with cognitive impairment who are being evaluated for Alzheimer's disease (AD) and other causes of cognitive decline. A negative scan indicates sparse to no neuritic plaques and is inconsistent with a neuropathologic diagnosis of AD.

pivotal_trials.design: Prospective, open-label, single-arm study evaluating diagnostic performance of Vizamyl PET imaging for detecting beta amyloid in the brain, using post-mortem histopathology as the truth standard, with images read independently by five blinded readers.
pivotal_trials.population: Patients 55 years of age or older diagnosed with terminal illnesses and a life expectancy of less than 1 year; 68 of 180 scanned died during the study and were evaluable at post-mortem.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Sensitivity of Vizamyl PET image interpretation (primary analysis) versus post-mortem histopathology truth standard, with specificity as secondary analysis.
pivotal_trials.result: Primary efficacy objective met: lower bound of 95% CI for sensitivity exceeded 70% for at least 3 of 5 readers; median sensitivity 88% (range 81-93%), median specificity 88% (range 44-92%).

pivotal_trials.design: Prospective pool-read study (enrolled no new subjects) using images from prior studies, read with the electronic self-training method to confirm sensitivity and specificity and to assess inter-reader and intra-reader reproducibility.
pivotal_trials.population: Subjects with a range of cognitive function, including those with and without a truth standard; primary analysis population of 135 subjects comprised 68 autopsy subjects, 36 biopsy subjects, and 31 young healthy volunteers.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Sensitivity and specificity of blinded visual interpretation (primary), with inter-reader and intra-reader reproducibility as secondary objectives.
pivotal_trials.n: 135 subjects in the primary analysis population (68 autopsy, 36 biopsy, 31 young healthy volunteers); 276 blinded visual interpretations of PET images were analyzed for reproducibility.
pivotal_trials.result: Met primary success criterion; sensitivity ranged 84% to 94% (median 92%) and specificity 77% to 96% (median 81%). Inter-reader agreement across all 5 readers was 81% with kappa 0.83 (95% CI 0.79, 0.86).

key_safety: Most commonly reported adverse reactions were flushing (16; 2%), increased blood pressure (10; 1%), headache (10; 1%), nausea (8; 1%), and dizziness (8; 1%) among 761 subjects. One subject experienced a serious hypersensitivity reaction with flushing, dyspnea, and chest pressure and recovered with treatment.
target_moa: Flutemetamol F 18 is a molecular imaging agent that binds to beta-amyloid plaques in the brain; the F-18 isotope produces a positron signal detected by a PET scanner. In vitro binding to postmortem human brain homogenates containing fibrillar beta-amyloid showed a dissociation constant (Kd) of 6.7 nM.

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee meeting was held; the clinical trial designs and efficacy endpoints for beta-amyloid-targeting radiopharmaceuticals had been established at prior Peripheral and Central Nervous System Drugs Advisory Committee meetings (October 23, 2008 and January 20, 2011).

description.text: Removed limitations of use and added indication for selecting patients indicated for amyloid beta-directed therapy, plus added quantitative image analysis

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for changes to the INDICATIONS AND USAGE section of the prescribing information by removing the limitations of use and adding a new indication, specifically, use for selection of patients who are indicated for amyloid beta-directed therapy as described in the prescribing information of the therapeutic products. In addition, the use of quantitative image analysis is added to the Image Display and Interpretation subsection of the DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION section.

summary.text: Vizamyl followed the established regulatory pathway for beta-amyloid PET imaging agents (similar to florbetapir F 18/Amyvid), with no advisory committee meeting held and a pediatric study requirement waived because the disease pathophysiology occurs only in adults. Approval was based on single-arm diagnostic-performance studies using post-mortem histopathology as the truth standard.

No advisory committee meeting was held. The clinical trial designs and efficacy endpoints for radiopharmaceutical imaging drugs that target βamyloid were established at meetings of the Peripheral and Central Nervous System Drugs Advisory Committee held on October 23, 2008 and on January 20, 2011. The Applicant followed this established regulatory path for the efficacy studies of flutemetamol F 18.

We are waiving the pediatric study requirement for this application because necessary studies are impossible or highly impracticable. The pathophysiology of the disease occurs only in the adult population.
